reason: DPS gives the U-shape only as background ('well-established', citing Cao, Jacobs & Ke 2024, which studies SPX options) and does not test it. The claim generalises it to all options. A peer-reviewed study of CBOE equity options (Chan, Chung & Johnson 1995, JFQA) found spreads that fall sharply after the open and then level off, with no U-shape. The pattern therefore depends on the market studied.
found: DPS: 'it is well-established that bid-ask spread follows a U-shaped pattern over the trading day, widening at the open and close (see, e.g., Cao, Jacobs, and Ke 2024)'. JFQA 1995 abstract: 'the options display a very different intraday pattern-one that declines sharply after the open, and then levels off.'
suggested_fix: SPX option spreads are described as roughly U-shaped through the day, widest at the open and again near the close (Cao, Jacobs & Ke 2024, as cited by Doshi, Pederzoli & Sert 2025). Older evidence on CBOE equity options instead shows spreads falling after the open and then levelling off (Chan, Chung & Johnson 1995).
